# Dev-only demo certs

These are self-signed, dev-only mTLS certs committed for demo convenience — `robot-edge`
and `operator-console` default to these exact paths, so a quick demo needs no `--cert`/
`--key`/`--ca` flags at all.

**Do not use in production, and do not treat these as secret.** They're generated by
[`tools/dev-certs`](../tools/dev-certs), never expire (`notBefore=1975`/`notAfter=4096`),
and are committed on purpose — anyone with this repo can already stand up either endpoint
with them. The CA's own private key (`dev-ca/ca.key`) is deliberately **not** committed
(see `.gitignore`), so a checkout of this repo can verify connections but can't mint new
trusted certs.

`robot/robot.crt`'s SAN includes `192.168.68.65` (the demo Pi's LAN IP *at the time
these were generated*) alongside the usual `robot-edge`/`localhost`/`127.0.0.1`. That
IP entry is vestigial and does **not** need regenerating when the Pi's address changes
(confirmed empirically across three different Pi IPs with this same cert) — both
binaries connect with `--server-name robot-edge`, which verifies against the `DNS:
robot-edge` SAN entry, not an IP match. See `xgo_bridge/RUNME.md` for the full
real-hardware run instructions, including why the Pi's IP changes on every reboot.

Only regenerate if you actually need a different DNS name/CA:

```bash
cargo run -p dev-certs -- --out-dir certs --robot-san <new-hostname>
```
